documents.unit: Faculty Senate / Teaching and Learning Commons
documents.title: Artificial Intelligence Syllabus Statement and Additional Sample AI Statements
documents.stance_why: The page gives a Faculty Senate default ("not allowed unless permission is given by an instructor") but mainly supplies "Additional Sample AI Statements" (two permissive, two restrictive) for instructors to choose from. Because it offers templates, the codebook says to set stance to delegates and list the tiers.
tiers: Default statement (AI not allowed without instructor permission)
Sample Permissive Statement One (coding/problem-solving help, cited)
Sample Permissive Statement Two (AI allowed with citation)
Sample Restrictive Statement One (no AI unless instructor says when)
Sample Restrictive Statement Two (proofreading ok; generated text not)
documents.summary: Faculty Senate page of optional syllabus statements. The AI entry sets a default of no AI without instructor permission, and four sample statements range from permissive to restrictive. Non-AI statements on the page were not coded.

documents.stance_why: The FAQ says "Students can only use artificial intelligence tools when allowed by instructors", though permission varies by program, course and assignment. Use is banned unless permitted, so restrict.
documents.summary: Student FAQ from the Office of Academic Integrity. It defines generative AI (including Grammarly), says use needs instructor permission, advises asking, citing and keeping transcripts, and explains the reasons in terms of learning and fair assessment.
